subsystems.name: X-ray source
subsystems.role: produces the primary beam that excites atoms in the rock.

subsystems.name: Focusing optic
subsystems.role: concentrates the beam to a spot roughly 100 µm across so individual mineral grains can be targeted.

subsystems.name: Positioning stage
subsystems.role: holds the instrument at a fixed standoff and scans the beam across the target in a raster.
parts: instrument turret on a robotic arm

subsystems.name: Detector
subsystems.role: measures the energy and count rate of fluorescent X-rays coming back from the sample.

subsystems.name: Context imager
subsystems.role: photographs the exact patch being measured so the chemistry can be tied to visible texture.

subsystems.name: Calibration and software
subsystems.role: turns raw counts into element concentrations.

buildSteps.title: Design the geometry
buildSteps.detail: Source, optic, detector and camera are laid out as a compact head that can face a rock without shadowing itself.

buildSteps.title: Build the X-ray tube
buildSteps.detail: A miniature tube is assembled and evacuated, with a high-voltage supply small enough to fly.

buildSteps.title: Draw the capillary lens
buildSteps.detail: Thousands of hollow glass capillaries are bundled and tapered so that X-rays glancing off their inner walls converge on one spot.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the detector
buildSteps.detail: A silicon drift detector and its front-end electronics are packaged for vacuum, vibration and thermal cycling.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the head
buildSteps.detail: Optic, tube, detector and camera are mounted on a hexapod that can scan the beam while holding standoff constant.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate on the ground
buildSteps.detail: The finished instrument is tested against rock standards of known composition to build a quantification model.

buildSteps.title: Qualify for spaceflight
buildSteps.detail: Vibration, thermal-vacuum and radiation testing prove it will survive launch and Mars.

buildSteps.title: Operate on the surface
buildSteps.detail: The arm places the head against a rock and rasters the beam; software fits the spectra into an elemental map.

prerequisites.why: a laboratory-scale source had to shrink to a few hundred grams.
they make a micro-focus spot possible without lenses that would absorb X-rays.
they resolve the closely spaced X-ray energies of neighbouring elements at low count rates.

prerequisites.tech: Robotic arm and turret with fine positioning
prerequisites.why: the instrument must sit within a fraction of a millimetre of the rock for hours.
the instrument must run on limited rover power and survive cosmic radiation.

pathway.milestone: PIXL mapping rocks on Mars inside Jezero crater, alongside cameras and other spectrometers
pathway.unlocks: element-by-element maps directly tied to visible rock texture.

pathway.milestone: returned samples analysed in terrestrial laboratories
pathway.unlocks: isotopic and trace-element detail far beyond what a rover can measure.

pathway.milestone: shrunken XRF heads on small rovers, drones and landers
pathway.unlocks: many more sites surveyed per mission.

pathway.milestone: in-situ elemental mapping for resource use on the Moon or Mars
pathway.unlocks: identifying ores, salts and water-bearing minerals where they will be needed.
